genesis.42.p1.b1.text: Why are you staring at one another?

genesis.42.p1.b2.text: “Look,” he added, “I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy some for us, so that we may live and not die.”

genesis.42.p1.b3.text: But Jacob did not send Joseph’s brother Benjamin with his brothers, for he said, “I am afraid that harm might befall him.”

genesis.42.p1.b4.text: So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt. … since the famine had also spread to the land of Canaan.

genesis.42.p2.b1.text: Now Joseph was the ruler of the land; he was the one who sold grain to all its people.

genesis.42.p2.b2.text: So when his brothers arrived, they bowed down before him with their faces to the ground.

genesis.42.p2.b3.text: Although Joseph recognized his brothers, they did not recognize him. Joseph remembered his dreams about them

genesis.42.p2.b4.text: You are spies! You have come to see if our land is vulnerable.

genesis.42.p3.b1.text: Not so, my lord, … Your servants have come to buy food. We are all sons of one man. Your servants are honest men,

genesis.42.p3.b2.text: Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, and one is no more.

genesis.42.p3.b3.text: … you shall not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.

genesis.42.p3.b4.text: So Joseph imprisoned them for three days,

genesis.42.p4.b2.text: I fear God. So do this and you will live:

genesis.42.p4.b3.text: If you are honest, leave one of your brothers in custody while the rest of you go and take back grain to relieve the hunger of your households.

genesis.42.p4.b4.text: Then bring your youngest brother to me so that your words can be verified, that you may not die.

genesis.42.p5.b1.text: Surely we are being punished because of our brother.

genesis.42.p5.b2.text: We saw his anguish when he pleaded with us, but we would not listen. That is why this distress has come upon us.

genesis.42.p5.b3.text: Didn’t I tell you not to sin against the boy? But you would not listen. …

genesis.42.p5.b4.text: They did not realize that Joseph understood them, since there was an interpreter between them.

genesis.42.p6.b1.text: And he turned away from them

genesis.42.p6.b3.text: When he turned back and spoke to them,

genesis.42.p6.b4.text: he took Simeon from them and had him bound before their eyes.

genesis.42.p7.b1.text: Then Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain, to return each man’s silver to his sack,

genesis.42.p7.b2.text: and they loaded the grain on their donkeys and departed.

genesis.42.p7.b3.text: My silver has been returned! … It is here in my sack.

genesis.42.p7.b4.text: What is this that God has done to us?

genesis.42.p8.b1.text: When they reached their father Jacob in the land of Canaan, they described to him all that had happened to them:

genesis.42.p8.b2.text: “The man who is lord of the land spoke harshly to us and accused us of spying on the country.

genesis.42.p8.b3.text: We are twelve brothers, … One is no more,

genesis.42.p8.b4.text: But bring your youngest brother back to me so I will know that you are not spies but honest men.

genesis.42.p9.b1.text: As they began emptying their sacks, there in each man’s sack was his bag of silver!

genesis.42.p9.b2.text: And when they and their father saw the bags of silver, they were dismayed.

genesis.42.p9.b3.text: You have deprived me of my sons. Joseph is gone and Simeon is no more. Now you want to take Benjamin.

genesis.42.p10.b1.text: You may kill my two sons if I fail to bring him back to you.

genesis.42.p10.b2.text: Put him in my care, and I will return him.

genesis.42.p10.b3.text: My son will not go down there with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left.

genesis.42.p10.b4.text: If any harm comes to him on your journey, you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.
